exposure: Number of umbilical cord entanglements: single vs multiple
Mode of delivery: emergent cesarean deliveries vs vaginal deliveries
Umbilical cord abnormalities: entanglements, number and location of loops, true knots, short cord
outcome: Neonatal outcome: low Apgar score, cord blood pH, respiratory distress, necrotizing enterocolitis, sepsis, transfusion, ventilation, seizure, hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy, phototherapy, death
cohort: 530 women who had emergent cesarean deliveries for non-reassuring fetal heart rate compared with 530 women who had vaginal deliveries, matched for maternal age, parity, and gestational age.
finding: Multiple umbilical cord entanglements, true knots, and short cords were more common in emergent cesarean deliveries for non-reassuring fetal heart rate and were associated with placental vascular lesions and adverse neonatal outcomes.
mod_finding: Multiple umbilical cord entanglements, true knots, and short cords were more common in emergent cesarean deliveries for non-reassuring fetal heart rate.
